articles.title: Championship roundup: Nuno admits West Ham ‘let down’ fans with Charlton defeat
articles.summary: Wolves sink teeth into Preston; Blackburn stun Boro. Southampton’s late show leaves Stoke pointless. Charlton maintained their perfect start to the Championship season with a 2-1 victory at West Ham in a pulsating London derby to pile more pressure on the Hammers manager, Nuno Espírito Santo.
body: Lloyd Jones and Tyreece Campbell put Charlton 2-0 ahead before Joel Piroe, signed on loan from Leeds, marked his first appearance for the home side with a goal that set up a frantic finish. Taty Castellanos then missed a stoppage-time penalty for West Ham that would have salvaged a point.
West Ham have not won their past 10 derbies, losing nine of them, but Hammers head coach Nuno defended the decision for Castellanos to take the spot-kick instead of Jarrod Bowen.

He said: “We trust Taty to take the penalties. I don’t know [if he will take the next one], we will have to decide. We started badly again. We got punished from a situation where we know Charlton create problems. It became much harder but we still created a lot of situations but were not accurate enough in the boxes. Football is this – to be accurate in the offensive box and we have to defend much better.
points: Wolves sink teeth into Preston; Blackburn stun Boro.

articles.title: European football: Inter start title defence with rout of promoted Monza
articles.summary: Second-half Esposito and Bisseck goals seal 4-1 win. Thauvin scores two as Lens put five past Auxerre. Inter kicked off their ⁠Serie A title defence with a 4-1 home win against ⁠ Monza, ​after the promoted side recovered from conceding an early ⁠goal to go in level at the break before the…
body: Hakan Calhanoglu ​put Inter ahead ‌in the ‌sixth minute, but the hosts were ‌far too complacent after taking the lead and Gustavo Varela equalised for the visitors just before the half-hour. Inter began the second half as ‌they had the first, with Piotr Zielinski scoring three minutes ​after the break, before Pio Esposito and Yann Bisseck wrapped up the win for Cristian Chivu’s side.
The England defender ⁠John Stones came on to make ​his ​Inter debut, with ​compatriots and fellow recent signings ​Djed Spence ‌and Curtis ​Jones ​watching on at San Siro.
Udinese drew 1-1 at home to Como in the other early game. Last season’s runners-up, Napoli, visit Genoa later on Saturday.

The Barcelona coach Hansi Flick said his new signing Rodri would not be involved in the Spanish champions’ La Liga opener against Elche on Sunday. The former Manchester City midfielder may be able to take part in their second match, against Athletic Bilbao, on Thursday. “He’s very concentrated, focused, our plan is that he will arrive on Monday with the team,” Flick said. “This is the plan. He’s a fantastic player, a leader, and his personality is very great.”

articles.title: Aston Villa upheaval is a risk but Emery can release v2.0 and reap rewards | Jonathan Wilson
articles.summary: After exodus of key players, youthful arrivals over the summer amount to a fresh beginning with plenty to get excited about. Last season was the greatest Aston Villa have enjoyed since they won the European Cup in 1982.
body: Despite a miserable start during which they failed to win any of their first five league games, there was even a spell around Christmas when it looked as though Villa might be challengers for the title. The question after a season like that is always: where next?

The answer is probably less clear now than it was amid the delirium of Istanbul in May. A reasonable consideration, even a couple of weeks ago, would have been: was that a one-off high, the limit of the club’s ambitions, or was there more? The danger for any team, but particularly one relatively unfamiliar with success, is to rest on its laurels, to be too loyal to those who have brought the long-awaited silverware.

It’s an understandable enough impulse: any transfer comes with a risk, so why make changes when what was there before worked? Why offload players to whom there is a sense of gratitude? Villa have not rested on their laurels.

articles.title: Kayode seals emphatic Brentford victory in wake-up call for sorry Spurs
articles.summary: Continue down this road and it will not be long before the chants of “Lincoln away” start up again. This was the start of Tottenham’s brave new era but there was no sign of any change.
body: If anything it was a reminder than winning the transfer window is not the same as winning on the pitch. There has been plenty of excitable predictions about Spurs, whose outlay will soon surpass £300m, but are they based on anything substantial? Not on the evidence of this game. There were no patterns of play from Spurs. They were timid in possession and chaotic at the back. They failed to perform the basics and they crumbled in the face of relentless pressing from Brentford, whose blend of power, speed and skill revealed a team determined to kick on in their second season under Keith Andrews.

Spurs could count themselves fortunate it finished 3-0. Brentford should have scored more – Igor Thiago, normally so reliable from the spot, marred an intelligent forward display by missing a penalty – but this was a joyous start to their campaign. Keane Lewis-Potter, Vitaly Janelt and Michael Kayode scored the goals and in the final analysis it was impossible not to dwell on a sparkling debut in midfield from Mamadou Sangaré, who already looks a bargain after joining from Lens for £39m.
points: Continue down this road and it will not be long before the chants of “Lincoln away” start up again.
This was the start of Tottenham’s brave new era but there was no sign of any change.

articles.title: Stokes stars as leaders Durham hammer Derbyshire
articles.summary: Ben Stokes hits 66 not out and takes 5-17 as Durham wrap up a 338-run victory at Derbyshire inside three days in Division Two of the County Championship.
body: An innings of the highest class from Ben McKinney, backed up by former England Test captain Ben Stokes with bat and ball, swept promotion favourites Durham to a crushing 338-run victory over Derbyshire in the County Championship.
McKinney showed why he is marked out as a future England Test player with 140 from 162 balls on the third day of the Division Two encounter at Derby.
The 21-year-old opener hit 15 fours and six sixes, dominating a second-wicket stand of 157 with Will Rhodes (52), followed by Stokes smashing an unbeaten 66 from 55 balls.
England off-spinner Shoaib Bashir took 3-77 before Durham declared on 295-6, setting Derbyshire a notional 423 for victory.

articles.title: 'Maybe people will stop sleeping on us' - Hull enjoy dream return
articles.summary: Relegation favourites Hull City start the season well with a victory over Manchester United as their manager says "we are trying to prove people wrong".
body: Hull City certainly managed to support their manager Sergej Jakirovic's desire as they shocked Manchester United - and many neutral observers - with a 2-0 win on their return to the Premier League.
The Tigers have been predicted by many to finish bottom, having only squeezed into the Premier League via last season's Championship play-offs.
After finishing third in the previous campaign, United were again being tipped to finish at least in the Champions League places.

But Jakirovic's side claimed a memorable first league win over United since a Second Division success in 1974 thanks to first-half goals from Semi Ajayi and fellow defender Nobel Mendy - one of 11 summer signings and with more to come.

articles.title: ‘I didn’t need it’ – Novak Djokovic reignites COVID-19 vaccine controversy with blunt admission
articles.summary: Novak Djokovic has reignited the COVID-19 vaccine debate after offering a blunt explanation for his decision not to get vaccinated, despite previously testing positive for the virus.
body: The 24-time Grand Slam champion refused to take the vaccine, a decision that led to his deportation from Australia in 2022 and the cancellation of his visa. At the time, Djokovic said he was not against vaccination but wanted to exercise his right to decide what he put into his body.

The decision resulted in him missing several high-profile tournaments, including the Australian Open and US Open in 2022, Indian Wells in 2022 and 2023, the Miami Open in 2022 and 2023, the Canadian Open in 2022 and the Cincinnati Masters in 2022.

Now, Djokovic has revisited the controversy in the Amazon Prime documentary Novak Djokovic: The Wolf in Winter, explaining why he decided against getting vaccinated despite having previously contracted COVID-19.
The Serbian icon claimed he did not believe he posed a threat to others because he had developed immunity and maintained that he had the freedom to make the decision himself.

articles.title: Jayden Oosterwolde Is the Latest Twist in Roma’s Transfer Saga
articles.summary: Late August is typically the most interesting point of silly season—not the most exciting, mind you, but the proximity to the new season makes every rumor and update feel more consequential.
body: The problem, as we see seemingly every year, is that negotiating for these second options is incredibly difficult, especially after Roma invested heavily in other positions. With a specific need to fill (in this case, left wing), little money to spend, and even less time to pull it off, the club has virtually no leverage in negotiations.

According to the latest rumors, Roma has abandoned its pursuit of Fofana (which I don’t believe for a second) and is instead focusing its efforts on Fenerbahçe’s Jayden Oosterwolde. While the 25-year-old Dutchman can’t fill the void left by Fofana, he’s a handy little full-back/center-back hybrid with ample top-flight experience, including nearly 90 appearances for Fenerbahçe over the past three seasons.

articles.title: Stokes stars as Durham thump Derbyshire to lift Championship promotion hopes
articles.summary: Ben Stokes starred again with bat and ball as Durham boosted their Rothesay County Championship promotion hopes with a crushing 338-run win at Derbyshire with a day to spare.
body: The former England captain followed up his half-century and two wickets in the first innings by making an unbeaten 66 before taking 5-17 as Derbyshire were skittled out for 84 while chasing an unlikely 423 for victory.
After resuming their first innings on 127-6, trailing by 156, Derbyshire were all out for 156, with Durham's Matthew Potts finishing with 5-46.
Durham opener Ben McKinney then made a brilliant 140 off 162 deliveries and Will Rhodes made 52 before a 55-ball 66 not out from Stokes saw the visitors declare on 295-6.
Stokes then took three wickets in four balls as Derbyshire's second innings capitulated, with Potts chipping in with 3-22.

articles.title: 😱 Tottenham collapse under De Zerbi: 3-0 v Brentford, Kinsky howler 👎
articles.summary: Roberto De Zerbi’s Tottenham crash badly on debut against Brentford: 3-0 thanks to goals from Lewis-Potter, Janelt and Kayode. A defeat that could have been even heavier, given that Igor Thiago missed a penalty with the result already beyond doubt.
body: Despite the €267 million spent in the summer (with another €87 million to be added for Savinho and, probably, more than €80 million for Marmoush ), Spurs' season has not started well.

The numbers tell the story of the match well: Brentford had 26 shots, 8 of them on target, compared to Tottenham's 9 overall (they also had 4 on target, but almost all of them were from Moore from the same position).

The first half was completely controlled by the Bees, who broke through Tottenham's defense with a fine team move: Sangaré drilled in a low cross for Lewis-Potter, who scored from the edge of the six-yard box.

The 2-0 came after Richarlison lost the ball in his own half, Jensen struck from distance and Kinsky's poor parry (promoted to first-choice goalkeeper despite last year's Champions League disaster ) allowed Janelt to score.

articles.title: Dundee claim derby bragging rights with victory over winless Dundee United
articles.summary: Dundee enjoyed another memorable trip across the road as they secured a deserved 2-0 derby victory away to Dundee United to move joint-top of the fledgling Scottish Premiership table.
body: Drey Wright opened the scoring late in the first half before Owen Bevan notched after the break as the Dark Blues made it three wins in their last four visits to Tannadice.

Steven Pressley's side are now level with Celtic and St Mirren on the six-point mark, albeit having played a game more than most of their rivals, after making it two wins from their opening three league matches.
By contrast, United endured a demoralising evening as they went down to a third straight defeat in all competitions to remain second-bottom with just one point from their three Premiership matches.
Terrors boss Jim Goodwin made six changes to the side that lost 4-0 to Celtic in the Premier Sports Cup, including restoring influential left-back Will Ferry after a minor injury.

articles.title: Sherrock claims first Women's Series title of 2026 in the absence of Greaves
articles.summary: Lisa Ashton and Fallon Sherrock shared the spoils at Events 17-18 of the PDC Women’s Series on Saturday, as the duo scooped a title each to reinforce their positions of second and third in the rankings respectively.
body: Leicester's Mattioli Arena played host to a double-header of Women's Series action, with Ashton and Sherrock celebrating success in Event 17 and 18.
Ashton stormed to the Event 17 crown, breezing to the last 16 with a trio of whitewash victories, before conceding just a solitary leg against Lauren Hall to reach the quarter-finals.
The Lancaster-based arrowsmith then saw off Grace Ferridge 5-1, although she faced a stern test against Gemma Hayter in the semi-finals, edging through a last-leg decider to reach the showpiece.
Nevertheless, the 2025 Women's World Matchplay champion swept aside Lauryn Salter with ease, triumphing 5-0 to lift her third Women's Series title of 2026.
